correctness.rationale: Marsiglietti–Melbourne Theorem 2.10 reduces the linear tail maximum under an expectation half-space to log-affine distributions on subintervals. Strict variance monotonicity of their mean and strict covariance monotonicity of the upper tail identify a unique mean-matched parameter. All fifteen possible interior integer means on support lengths three through seven have exact positive H and negative D rational witnesses, verified by verify.py; these imply strict upper-tail probability below one half. Reflection supplies the lower-tail counterpart. For eight support points, exact signs at rational endpoints bracket the unique mean-five parameter, and an exact positive D at the lower endpoint forces an upper-tail majority. The proof is not a finite-experiment extrapolation; dependence on the independently published localization theorem is explicit.

originality.rationale: The sharp minimality claim is different from the documented eight-point failure in Alqasem et al. (arXiv:2208.12702, Corollary 1.4 and its succeeding example): their example shows existence at eight, not impossibility below eight. The Marsiglietti–Melbourne localization theorem (arXiv:2004.12005, Theorem 2.10) covers the reduction to log-affine extremizers but does not give the fifteen exact small-support sign checks. The published global \(e^{-1}\) bound does not imply the length-seven half-mass theorem. Searches for mean-as-median, seven-point, eight-point, truncated-geometric and sharp support threshold equivalents did not identify covering literature. Priority is not certified: an equivalently stated earlier theorem remains possible, notably in a related 2024 dissertation available only through its abstract.

value.rationale: The motivating 2022 work explicitly demonstrates failure of the universal one-half integer-mean claim at eight atoms, making the first possible support length an intrinsic, sharply defined invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The answer eight is complete and exact, with universal protection up to seven proved using a structural localization result plus a finite exhaustive rational certificate. This clarifies when mean/median coincidence survives under discrete log-concavity and gives a natural boundary to a half-mass improvement of the Feige-type deviation inequality. The contribution is the sharp boundary, not the known eight-point example alone or the known localization theorem.
